    Dice Control Pro

    User Manual SRR TRACKER · VERSION 1.0

    Dice Control Pro is a practice tracker for controlled dice throwers. Log every roll, and it works out your sevens to rolls ratio (SRR), shows how your dice landed against the set you threw, and prices every craps bet from your own rolls. A built-in betting table lets you play a bankroll with Las Vegas payouts while you practice. Everything stays on your device: no account, no cloud and no tracking.

    RUNS ONAny phone or computer browser
    DICE SETSHardway, 3V, 2V, Yo and more
    BETTING TABLELas Vegas payouts

    I want to…

    • Log my rolls
    • Pick my dice set
    • Start a bankroll
    • See what each bet pays
    • Understand off and on
    • See the house edge with odds
    • Read my SRR and stats
    • Back up my data

    1Getting Started

    Dice Control Pro opens on the Roll screen. The big number at the top is your SRR, your sevens to rolls ratio: total rolls divided by sevens. Random dice throw a seven on 6 of the 36 combinations, an SRR of 6.0. A thrower who keeps the dice together and on axis throws fewer sevens, so the higher your SRR above 6.0, the better.

    The five screens

    The bar along the bottom moves between the screens:

    ScreenWhat it's for
    RollYour SRR, the betting table, and the dice buttons you tap to log each roll.
    SetThe dice set you are throwing: Hardway, 3V, 2V, All Sevens, Yo, Straight Sixes, Crossed Sixes or your own.
    StatsSRR, your edge on each bet, hands, come-out and point, how the dice landed, and the totals you rolled.
    SessionsSaved sessions, comparing sets, CSV export and backups.
    OptionsButton size, betting table settings, Las Vegas odds or your own odds limit, and more.
    PRIVATE BY DESIGN

    Your rolls are stored only in the browser on the device you use. Nothing is uploaded. Use Backup to keep a safe copy or move your data to another phone or computer.

    2The Roll Screen

    The top of the Roll screen sums up the session you are throwing now.

    ItemWhat it shows
    SRRRolls divided by sevens, with a gauge from 4.0 to 9.0. The tick marks random dice at 6.0.
    Rolls and sevensHow many rolls you have logged, how many were sevens, and your seven percentage next to random's 16.7%.
    Rolls since last 7How long the current run has gone without a seven.
    VerdictThe luck check: how often random dice would match your SRR. A small sample shows "Too few rolls to judge". As rolls build it moves to "Promising, keep logging" and then "Strong evidence of an edge".
    PuckOFF while coming out, ON with the point number once a point is set. Below it you see the hand in progress.
    SetThe dice set in use. Tap Change set to switch.
    TIP

    Turn off the luck check in Options if you would rather not see the verdict while you throw.

    3Logging Rolls

    Log each roll in the Log a roll box on the Roll screen. There are two ways to log:

    • Dice faces: tap the face showing on the left die, then the right die. The roll logs as soon as both are picked. Faces tell the app whether the dice stayed on axis, so this is the mode to use for the Axis and pitch stats and hardway bets.
    • Totals only: tap the total. It's faster, but totals can't show how the dice landed, so those rolls count toward SRR only.

    Undo and save

    Undo last roll removes the last roll. With the betting table on, it also puts your bets and bankroll back exactly as they were before that roll.

    Save session and start new files the session on the Sessions screen and starts a fresh one with the same set. Any bets still on the betting table come back to your rack.

    Session notes

    Type anything you want to remember about the session, such as the table, grip or how you felt. The notes are saved with the session and appear in your history and CSV export.

    The roll tape

    The row of numbers under the dice buttons is the roll tape: the last 24 rolls of the session, newest first. The big number is the total and the small numbers are the left die · right die, so 9 5·4 means the left die showed 5 and the right die 4.

    MarkingMeaning
    Gold outlineA zero-pitch hit: both dice landed exactly as set, with no rotation. On the Hardway set it always comes up a pair (2·2, 3·3, 4·4, 5·5).
    Solid redA seven-out.
    Red outlineA seven on the come-out (a winner for the pass line).
    White outlineThe point was made.
    Dashed outlineA come bet was down on that roll, under the pass and come bet plan.

    4Choosing Your Dice Set

    Open the Set screen to choose the set you are throwing. Each set keeps its own SRR and stats, so you can compare sets fairly.

    SetNotes
    HardwayHardways on every face around the axis. Pick 3, 2, 4 or 5 as the top face.
    3V and 2VThe classic V sets.
    All SevensSevens on all four sides, used on the come-out.
    YoLeft die 5 up with 6 facing you, right die 6 up with 5 facing.
    Straight Sixes and Crossed SixesSixes sets for the point cycle.
    CustomAny set you build yourself.

    Building or adjusting a set

    • Pick the top face and the face toward you for each die.
    • Tap a top die, or use Turn whole die ¼, to rotate that whole die a quarter turn.
    • "Facing you" is the side toward the shooter. "Far side" is the side toward the back wall.
    • Tap Use this set. Choosing a different set saves the current session and starts a new one, so each set keeps its own SRR.

    5The Betting Table & Bankroll

    The betting table sits on the Roll screen just above Log a roll. Bet chips with a bankroll, then log your rolls: every bet on the table is paid or taken on each roll, just like at a casino. You can turn the table off in Options.

    Starting a bankroll

    • Tap $100, $200, $500, $1,000 or $5,000, or type your own amount.
    • Tap Start with this bankroll.
    • To start over, tap Change bankroll at the top of the table. Your chips come back, the table clears and your win or loss resets. Your rolls and SRR are not touched.

    Your bankroll tiles

    TileShows
    In your rackChips you can still bet, and what you started with.
    On the tableEverything you have down, including any dealers' bet.
    Win or lossUp or down since you started the bankroll, and for this session.
    Dealers' betsWhat you have bet for the dealers, and what they collected.

    Chips and the three modes

    Pick a chip, $1 (white), $5 (red), $25 (green) or $100 (black), then tap a spot on the layout. The buttons next to the chips set what a tap does:

    ModeTapping a bet…
    AddAdds the selected chip to that bet.
    Take downTakes that one bet back to your rack. Everything else stays up. Pass line and dealers' bets can't come down once a point is set.
    Off / OnCalls the bet off: it stays on the table with no action until you tap it again. See Calling Bets Off.

    Take down all bets you can clears everything that's allowed to come down in one tap.

    6Bets & Payouts

    The table pays Las Vegas odds. Payouts are rounded down to the dollar, like a real table pays.

    BetPaysHouse edge
    Pass line, come, dealers' betEven money1.41%
    Odds (pass or come)True odds: 2 to 1 on 4/10, 3 to 2 on 5/9, 6 to 5 on 6/80%
    Place 6 and 87 to 61.52%
    Place 5 and 97 to 54.00%
    Place 4 and 109 to 56.67%
    FieldEven money; 2 pays double, 12 pays triple2.78%
    Hard 6 and 89 to 19.09%
    Hard 4 and 107 to 111.11%
    All Small, All Tall34 to 1 (or 30 to 1)7.8%
    Make 'Em All175 to 1 (or 150 to 1)7.5%

    Las Vegas table rules

    • Odds limit: 3-4-5x: up to 3x your flat bet on the 4 and 10, 4x on the 5 and 9, 5x on the 6 and 8. Turn off Las Vegas odds in Options to set your own limit.
    • Off on the come-out: place bets, hardways and come odds don't work on the come-out unless you call them on.
    • Pass line bets go down on the come-out. Once a point is set, use the come.
    • Winning place, hardway, field and pass line bets stay up; you're paid the win. Winning come bets and odds come back to your rack.
    • Hardways need dice faces. With Totals only, a 4, 6, 8 or 10 doesn't decide a hardway, but a 7 still loses it.

    Rounding: bet in the right amounts

    Because the table pays whole dollars, some amounts lose a little to rounding. A $5 place bet on the 6 pays $5 (it works out to $5.83); a $6 bet pays $7 in full. Bet place 6 and 8 in multiples of $6, and place 5 and 9 in multiples of $5.

    Even odds on the 5 and 9

    Odds on the 5 and 9 pay 3 to 2, so an odd amount loses the half dollar. When your odds on the 5 or 9 are an odd amount, an orange warning appears and the odds spot shows MAKE IT EVEN. Add a dollar and it goes away.

    Every payout explained

    After each roll, the results under the table list what won and lost. Every win shows the math, for example "Place 6 $12 at 7 to 6 pays $14", and whether your bet stays up or comes back to your rack. When the table rounds down, it shows what you lost to rounding.

    7Come Bets, Reminders & Off and On

    The come bet plan

    With Pass and come bet tracking on, the app follows a simple plan: a pass line bet, then come bets until two are on numbers. A come bet that wins is replaced. Once all three bets are up, every number that hits counts as a win, and after your set number of wins (2 by default) one more come bet goes down. When all six numbers are covered, one more come bet goes down too.

    Come bet reminders

    When a come bet is due, the COME bar on the layout turns gold and pulses, and a gold box under the table tells you how many come bets you have up and how many the plan calls for. The line by the dice buttons says Come bet this roll. Both follow the chips actually on your table, and both clear as soon as you put a chip in the come.

    Off and on

    When you have a come bet on a number and a new come bet in the come box, and that number rolls, the dealer doesn't move anything. That is called off and on:

    • Your come bet stays on the number, and its odds stay up and working.
    • Your new come bet stays in the come box for the next roll.
    • You're paid just the win: the flat bet at even money plus the odds at true odds.
    EXAMPLE

    $5 come bet on the 5 with $6 odds, $5 in the come, and a 5 rolls: you win $14 ($5 even money plus $9 for the odds at 3 to 2). The $5 and $6 stay on the 5, and your $5 stays in the come.

    8Calling Bets Off & Taking Them Down

    Take down one bet

    Tap Take down, then tap the one bet you want back. Only that bet comes back to your rack.

    Call a bet off before a roll

    • Tap Off / On, then tap a bet. It shows "off" and gets no action, win or lose, until you tap it again.
    • You can call off odds (pass or come), place bets, hardways and the field. Pass line, dealers' and come bets on numbers always work.
    • If odds are off when the shooter sevens out, they come back to your rack. If the number hits while they're off, they come back unpaid.
    • On the come-out, tapping a place bet, hardway or come odds calls it on (working), and it shows "on".
    • Call all my bets off turns off everything that can be called off. When all are off, the same button turns them back on.

    Bets you call off stay off roll after roll until you turn them back on.

    9All Tall All Small

    A row of three bets above the pass line:

    BetWins when…Pays
    All Small2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 all roll before a 734 to 1 (30 to 1)
    All Tall8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 all roll before a 734 to 1 (30 to 1)
    Make 'Em AllEvery number 2 to 12 except 7 rolls before a 7175 to 1 (150 to 1)
    • These bets open only when the board is clear: at the start, or right after any 7. Once the dice roll, the row locks until the next 7.
    • Number dots under All Small and All Tall turn gold as each number rolls.
    • Any 7, even on the come-out, loses all three and clears the board.
    • Pick the 34 · 175 or 30 · 150 payouts in Options to match your casino.

    10The Dealers' Bet

    The DEALERS spot is a pass line bet you make for the dealers on the come-out, a common way to tip at the table.

    • It wins and loses with the pass line.
    • When it wins, the dealers keep the bet and the win. When it loses, the bet is gone.
    • The Dealers' bets tile shows how much you have bet for them and how much they collected.
    • The dealers' bet is left out of the house edge figures, since that money is a tip.

    11House Edge & Odds

    Odds bets pay true odds, so the house has no edge on them. Every dollar of odds you put behind a pass or come bet spreads the 1.41% edge on the flat bet over more money, so the edge on what you have down drops.

    On the layout

    • Meter: the bar at the top of the table shows the house edge on everything you have down, with ▼ down or ▲ up as it changes. A tick marks the pass line alone at 1.41%.
    • Each spot shows its own house edge in small type.
    • With odds: a pass line or come bet with odds shows the old edge crossed out and the new one in gold, for example 1.41% 0.47% with odds.
    $5 pass line plus…House edge
    No odds1.41%
    $5 odds0.71%
    $10 odds0.47%
    $15 odds0.35%
    $25 odds (5x on the 6 or 8)0.24%
    $50 odds (10x)0.13%

    Odds edge calculator

    $
    $
    House edge0.24%

    The edge box

    Under your bankroll tiles, the edge box lists what you have down and the blended house edge. Once you have logged 36 rolls with your current set, it also prices the same bets from your own rolls, so you can see your edge, not just the house's. Under 5,000 rolls, treat that figure as a rough guide.

    Don't want to see the edge? Turn off House edge on the table in Options.

    Your own odds limit

    Turn off Las Vegas odds in Options and pick 1x, 2x, 5x, 10x, 20x or 100x, or type your own limit up to 1000x. It applies to every number, for pass line and come odds. The odds spot shows the limit, the meter keeps dropping as you add odds, and the Stats edge row is renamed to match, for example "Pass or come + 100x odds".

    12Stats

    The Stats screen breaks down the set you are throwing. Choose This session or All time at the top. All time counts only sessions thrown with the same set.

    SRR and the luck check

    Your SRR, rolls and sevens, with the luck check: how often random dice would throw an SRR this good. The fewer the rolls, the more a hot or cold streak can be luck.

    Your edge

    Your edge on each bet, worked out from the share of each total you actually threw:

    • House: the edge against a random shooter.
    • Yours: the same bet priced from all your rolls.
    • Without on-axis 7s: leaves out sevens thrown with both dice on axis, to show what those sevens cost you. It is not your real edge.

    The Pass or come + odds row assumes full odds behind every point at your odds limit. Hardway rows use only rolls logged with dice faces.

    Come-out and point

    Point-cycle SRR counts only rolls made with a point on, divided by seven-outs. Come-out sevens are winners, so they are left out. You also see points made, come-out 7s and 11s, and come-out craps, each next to random.

    Hands

    A hand runs from the first come-out roll to the seven-out. You see hands finished, average hand, longest hand and the hand in progress. Saving a session ends the hand in progress without counting it in the average.

    Pass and come bets

    How the come bet plan would have done with your rolls: pass line won and lost, come bets, come numbers hit, wins counted, extra come bets added and net units.

    Number targets

    Pick the numbers you aim for, such as 6 and 8. You see how often you hit them against random, and how many target hits you get per seven.

    Axis and pitch

    From rolls logged with dice faces, how the dice landed compared with your set:

    ResultMeaning
    Zero pitchBoth dice show the faces you set (on Hardway: 2·2, 3·3, 4·4, 5·5).
    Single pitchOne face apart.
    Double pitchTwo faces apart. On the Hardway set this is where on-axis sevens come from.
    One die off axisAn axis face on one die only.
    Both dice off axisAxis faces on neither die.

    Each bar shows your share next to what random dice would show. More on-axis results mean the dice stayed together in the air.

    Where your sevens came from

    How many of the six ways to roll a seven fall in each axis and pitch group for your set, and how many of your sevens came from each.

    Totals rolled

    A chart of every total from 2 to 12. The line on each bar is what random dice would show, and the count is under each total.

    HOW MANY ROLLS?

    A few hundred rolls can swing a lot by luck. The app labels small samples, and figures from fewer than 5,000 rolls with a set are a rough guide.

    13Sessions & Comparing Sets

    Saved sessions

    Every saved session shows its set, date, rolls, sevens, hands and longest hand, your notes and its SRR. With the betting table on, it also shows your bankroll result and dealers' bets. Tap Delete to remove one.

    Compare sets

    Every set you have thrown side by side: rolls, SRR, how often the dice stayed on axis and average hand. The set in use is in gold.

    14Export & Backup

    ButtonWhat it does
    Download rolls as CSVEvery roll from every session, with its set, how the dice landed, come-out or point and your notes. Opens in Excel or Google Sheets.
    Copy all rolls as CSVThe same data copied, ready to paste into a sheet or email.
    Download backupOne file with everything: all sessions, the current one, your sets, notes and options.
    Restore from a backup fileLoads a backup, for example to move your data to another phone or computer.
    BEFORE YOU ERASE

    Erase all rolls and sessions in Options can't be undone. Download a backup first if you might want your data later.

    NEW DEVICE OR BROWSER?

    Your data lives in one browser on one device. To move it, use Download backup on the old one, then Restore from a backup file on the new one.

    16Tips & Tricks

    1Log faces, not totals

    Dice faces show whether the dice stayed on axis and decide hardway bets. Use Totals only when you need speed.

    2One set per session

    Each set keeps its own SRR. Switching sets saves the session, so your numbers never mix.

    3Bet the right amounts

    Place 6 and 8 in $6s, 5 and 9 in $5s, and odds on the 5 and 9 in even amounts, so nothing is lost to rounding.

    4Watch the meter

    Add odds and watch the house edge fall. With full 3-4-5x odds, it drops to about 0.37%.

    5Use Large buttons

    At a practice rig, Large dice buttons are easier to hit between throws.

    6Back up often

    Your data lives in one browser. Download a backup now and then and keep it somewhere safe.

    7Be patient with SRR

    A few hundred rolls can be luck. Keep logging, and trust the figures as you head toward 5,000 rolls.

    8Undo mistakes

    Tapped the wrong face? Undo last roll puts the roll, your bets and your bankroll back.

    17About Dice Control Pro

    Dice Control Pro is a practice and tracking tool for controlled dice throwers, built by JohnBobApps, a one‑person studio making privacy‑first tools for casino players.

    The betting table is a simulation for practice only. No real money is bet, won or lost.

    Your data is yours.

    Every roll, session, set and note stays in your browser on your device. Dice Control Pro has no accounts, no cloud sync and no tracking, and it never shares anything with anyone.
